name: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC)

sections.title: Quarterly revenue
sections.callout: 2026 outlook: TSMC expects revenue growth of close to 30% in US-dollar terms and capital spending of up to about US$56B.

footnotes: TSMC is a foreign private issuer and files Form 20-F, not a 10-K. Figures are in New Taiwan dollars (NT$) from its audited 2025 consolidated financial statements; US-dollar revenue is as reported by TSMC.

Net income is attributable to shareholders of the parent. General & administrative is shown net of NT$0.4B of other operating income. Free cash flow = operating cash flow − acquisitions of property, plant & equipment (calculated).
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: TSMC's revenue grew 31.6% to a record NT$3,809.1B in 2025 (US$122.4B, up 35.9%), driven by demand for AI chips. Advanced nodes of 7nm and below made up 74% of wafer revenue, up from 69%. Gross margin rose to 59.9% and operating margin to 50.8%.
Net income rose 46.4% to NT$1,717.9B, or NT$66.25 per share. TSMC spent US$40.9B on capital expenditures and still generated NT$1,002.6B of free cash flow, while paying NT$466.8B in dividends.
highlights: Q4 2025 revenue reached a record NT$1,046.1B, up 20.5%.
3nm and 5nm together made up 60% of wafer revenue.
watch: Capital spending is set to rise to up to about US$56B in 2026.
High-performance computing made up 55% of Q4 2025 revenue, so results lean heavily on AI and data-center demand.
Figures are in NT$, so US-dollar results also depend on the exchange rate.
TSMC files a 20-F, which has different disclosure rules than a 10-K.
